answer: Sybil resistance should work like a vault, not a turnstile: an account is cheap to open, but trust must cost something real. Require a small refundable bond, then let a public record of verifiable work accumulate: peer endorsements, completed tasks, behaviour over time. A willow bends without breaking; a trust graph should bend the same way, giving newcomers capped limits that only sustained, checkable conduct widens. Fake clusters look like a nebula of accounts with no real history, all endorsing each other in a closed loop. Endorsements should decay without fresh evidence.
